why: Hard angular seams in the intro cutscene's ocean -- the lighter sheen ends on straight polygon edges leaving darker flat regions. The water is placed tiles of two submodels (an opaque blue base and a MIX-blended sheen 0.19 above it, both type 0x01 textured) under a scrolled texture at a grazing angle; the port divided S and T by Q per VERTEX and gave the engine u / v with q = 1, so the texture was interpolated affinely per triangle where the GS interpolates S, T, Q linearly and divides per pixel. Fix: the vertex carries the GS's Q (engine ps2e_draw_vertex.q, PS2E_DRAW_HAS_VERTEX_Q) and the port hands S, T, Q through -- perspective-correct texturing for every model, sky and skin draw. The judge: no thin (< 4 px) straight luminance edge (Sobel > 6 luminance/px) longer than the oracle's own longest x 1.5 (at least 48 px; frozen 96 px without the oracle frames) inside the water below the horizon's sheen band, at presents 1340 and 1620.
